about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2020 only.

rows.detail: New in FY2020 with a $0.00 opening balance: 'Cares Act Funding - COVID' $147,421.00 received / $15,428.26 spent / $131,992.74 carried; 'FEMA #4496 - COVID Grant' $0 received / $34,094.82 spent / ($34,094.82) i.e. a NEGATIVE carry-forward; 'Continuity of Operations Grant' $35,000; 'MIIA Flex Grant' $6,616; 'Financial Trend Monitoring Grant' $15,000; 'Extended Polling Hours Grant' $1,248.80; 'Municipal Vulnerability Grant' $15,000; 'Recycling IQ Grant' $10,929.05; 'State Earmark - Town Hall Ramp' $13,500 received against $27,000 spent, also negative.

rows.detail: Also states 534 fire prevention inspections were conducted and a $6,953 Department of Fire Services grant continued.

The Public Access Cable committee's own revenue-vs-expenses table carries a figure copied forward unchanged from the FY2019 report: the 'Subtotal' of $449,041.36 is FY2019's number, and does not follow from FY2020's own arithmetic ($699,875.47 - $116,933.54 = $582,941.93). The two expense totals on the same page also disagree by 32 cents.

rows.table: Public Access Cable FY20 line item expenses and revenue vs expenses
rows.detail: ARITHMETIC WORTH CHECKING: the expenses total is given as $116,933.22 in the line-item table and $116,933.54 in the revenue-vs-expenses table, a 32-cent discrepancy; and $699,875.47 - $116,933.54 = $582,941.93, not the $449,041.36 printed as 'Subtotal' -- the $449,041.36 figure is carried over unchanged from the FY2019 report's version of this same table, where it was correct.

The Presidential Primary results are PRINTED TWICE -- pages 189-191 are byte-identical to pages 193-195, and only the second printing has its header page (192). Anyone summing vote totals across the elections section will double-count. The table of contents does not acknowledge it.

rows.table: Presidential Primary Election, 3 March 2020
rows.detail: THIS RESULT IS PRINTED TWICE IN THE REPORT.

rows.table: Presidential Primary Election, 3 March 2020
rows.detail: Pages 193, 194 and 195 are byte-identical to pages 189, 190 and 191; the only difference is that the second printing has its own header page (192) carrying the Democratic presidential preference results, which the first printing lacks.

rows.table: Combined balance sheet, all fund types and account groups, 30 June 2020
rows.detail: Note the FY19-and-older real estate receivable lines are identical to FY2019's report, which is what you would expect for stale receivables.

rows.table: Table of contents
rows.detail: The listed page numbers are reliable EXCEPT for the election section: the contents say 'Special State Primary Election March 3, 2020 ... 188-191' and 'Presidential Primary Election March 3, 2020 ... 192-195', but page 188 holds the Special State Primary AND a Special State Election, and pages 189-191 already hold Presidential Primary results, which are then reprinted on 192-195.

The FY2021 capital plan appears in FOUR different total amounts inside this one report: $1,329,133 as recommended in January, $664,800 as re-voted by the committee in April after the shutdown, $647,880 as actually voted in June, and a further $494,333 voted at the November Special Town Meeting. The page that prints the $1,329,133 table explains the other figures in prose but does not print the revised list.

COVID appears as named funds on the balance sheet, not just in narrative: 'Cares Act Funding - COVID' ($147,421 received) and 'FEMA #4496 - COVID Grant' both appear in the special revenue funds table with a $0.00 opening balance, and the FEMA grant closes the year at NEGATIVE $34,094.82 -- $34,094.82 spent against nothing received.
The Board of Health's own case count for the first pandemic year is a single line in a disease list: 'SARS CoV-2 (COVID-19)...355'. In the same list influenza fell from 380 the previous year to 63.

The Building Department's page (53) is essentially EMPTY in extraction -- only '185 Gas Permits' survives out of what in FY2019 was a five-line permit count. This is an extraction gap, not an absence of data, and it is easy to mistake for the latter.

The Police Chief attributes the year's crime changes to the pandemic but explicitly hedges it: 'Without a significant study being conducted, it is believed that the number of assaults that have occurred is related to the Pandemic and the effects of isolation.' The report separates the measurement from the explanation, which the financial sections generally do not.

Turnout for the pandemic-delayed Annual Town Election on 20 June 2020 was 524 ballots from 8,088 registered voters -- 6.5% -- against 7,224 from 8,566 (84.3%) at the November state election five months later, in the same report.

The New Growth Revenue table (p38) has no counterpart in the FY2019 report, and its tax-rate column is offset by a year from the fiscal year on the same row (FY2020 new growth shown at the 18.68 FY2019 rate). The page does not say whether that is deliberate.
The Monty Tech AP table's own last column contradicts the prose above it: the table says 75 of 106 exams (71%) qualified while the paragraph says '89 out of 146 (61%) exams earned qualifying credit'.

rows.table: Monty Tech Advanced Placement participation and results, Spring 2016 to Spring 2020
rows.detail: WORTH CHECKING: the last two rows disagree -- 75 qualifying exams out of 106 total exams is 71%, but 146 test takers taking only 106 exams is implausible, and the prose above says '89 out of 146 (61%) exams earned qualifying credit', which contradicts both.
